identity.real_world_identity_notes: Group C prototype campaigned by Nissan in 1989, powered by the VRH35 3,496cc twin-turbo DOHC V8. The chassis was built by Lola Cars International after Nissan switched from March Engineering for that season, so the chassis constructor is identity context rather than the marque. Nissan's heritage record specifies a VGC five-speed transmission, matching the five forward gears exercised in the live drive.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behavior was directly observed in a guided drive with automatic clutch and shifting disabled.
Upshift throttle lift and downshift manual blip are set from the guided-drive method notes: the upshift was accepted after a lift and the downshift after the driver's own blip.

The gearbox is modeled as a dog-engagement racing box from the manufacturer's VGC specification together with the observed clutchless running shifts. The H-pattern layout is not established and stays unknown.
'Nissan R89C - Low Downforce' inherits these verified base controls as an approved aero-package assumption and was not separately live-tested.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.nissan-r89c.20260813t050039446z-0de58672 by Jason Kinslow.
'Nissan R89C - Low Downforce' is an exact observed identity inheriting the verified base controls; that aero configuration was not separately live-tested.

confidence.basis: Simulator behavior was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the manufacturer heritage record independently establishes the real-world identity and the five-speed VGC transmission.

claims.basis: Nissan's own heritage record establishes the 1989 identity, engine, and Lola-built chassis, and the exact simulator identity was observed live.

The manufacturer specifies a VGC five-speed transmission and the live drive confirmed five forward gears with H-pattern actuation. VGC is a racing transaxle and the drive accepted clutchless running shifts, which is consistent with dog engagement; the H-pattern layout, standard versus dogleg, is not established and stays unknown.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.
The guided drive recorded that a clutchless upshift was accepted after a throttle lift and a clutchless downshift after the driver's manual throttle blip, with no automatic cut or blip detected.

driver_summary: Nissan specifies a Hewland VGC five-speed, a racing dog box, so blip every downshift to be safe. The gearbox is established, but whether a blip is needed to engage the gear was never tested.

deviations.basis: Whether the driver must blip on downshifts is not established. A guided drive settles what the simulator requires; where the real car differs, that difference is recorded as an override rather than changing this value.

The gate is not established. It is read from the cockpit by watching the lever and the driver's hand through a shift, the method that read three dogleg gates in dataset 0.3.28 and that registered sources then corroborated.
Whether the car needs a throttle lift on upshifts is not established. A guided drive settles it, by holding the throttle through an upshift and seeing whether the gear engages.

notes: 'Nissan R89C - Low Downforce' is an exact approved alias whose controls are inherited from the verified base; it has not been separately live-tested.
